title: Resident machines: state, events, publication and readiness
summary: An explicit ancestry pass through the recent resident-state machine line. The foundation atlas already contains the repository-declared AnttisNeuron/GrowingAnttisNeuron lineage into ActiveVectorNN and NewMachine; this pass adds AnttisBrain2 as the rendering ancestor of HorizonNet and groups the surviving resident-state/publication ideas without inventing a NewMachine→FusionMachine ancestry edge.

nodes.claim: A dependency-free WebGL raymarching game whose apparently infinite mirror recursion is truncated at the observer's resolution horizon; the same principle is explicitly identified as the origin of HorizonNet.
nodes.survived: A practical rendering rule: recursive structure can be generated by a contracting operator and stopped when remaining structure falls below the observer's resolution. The repo also records a useful engineering lesson that continuous parameterized geometry can replace branch-heavy shader shape code.
nodes.killed: The later HorizonNet autopsy shows that translating the mirror truncation directly into fixed-point neural halting changes the problem: the renderer truncates an observer-invisible transient, while a recurrent network may still be doing useful computation before state convergence.

edges.why: Both repositories explicitly state that HorizonNet came from AnttisBrain2's four-bounce recursive-mirror / observation-horizon rendering trick.

motifs.title: Resident computation is not the same thing as publication
motifs.description: Across the recent machine line, internal state is allowed to persist while outward influence becomes a separate sparse event. NewMachine then separates state repair from publication, and FusionMachine pushes relevance even later without claiming that current relevance should rewrite the resident world state.

motifs.title: An observer horizon moved from a renderer into inference—and broke usefully
motifs.description: AnttisBrain2's mirror recursion really is limited by pixel resolution. HorizonNet imports that intuition into recurrent inference, where the autopsy discovers that state convergence and decision completion are not the same horizon.

motifs.title: State, reliability, relevance and route identity separate
motifs.description: AnttisNeuron/GrowingAnttisNeuron supply persistent physical modes and operator identity; ActiveVectorNN separates state from events; NewMachine separates reliability repair from publication; FusionMachine tests the stronger hypothesis that current relevance should often be applied after resident world dynamics.
